## Context

This is a scoped follow-up to #1 and the implementation in draft PR #2. The source snapshot is commit `9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8`; it is not a claim that the default branch already contains that work. Coordinate the implementation baseline with PR #2 or its merged successor. Issue creation and the ready-for-agent label do not authorize provider launches, trust/permission changes, audit adoption, billing changes or new spending. Follow the execution host’s current policy and preserve existing evidence.

## Triage evidence

- Confirmed static raw-capture-to-report-to-persistence and error-propagation paths. No fresh canary execution or actual secret leakage is claimed.
- An existing safe native-error projection and artifact binding checks are present, so this task must extend the relevant boundary rather than discard provenance or valid results.

**Redundancy check:** Inspected provider capture/reporting, wrapper persistence, journal/cancellation propagation and existing safe native error projection. Existing related mechanisms do not satisfy the specific remaining contract below.

**Prior rejection check:** No rejection knowledge base or matching rejection record was present in the inspected checkout. No other follow-up issue existed at triage start.

## Dated source references

- [Provider report data flow](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/src/pilot/provider-session.ts)
- [Host report persistence](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/src/pilot/host-wrapper.ts)
- [Existing safe error projection](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/src/pilot/allowance.ts)
- [Report binding and cleanup verification](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/src/pilot/context-driver.ts)
- [Journal event persistence](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/src/pilot/journal.ts)

The agent-brief comment is the implementation contract. Parent #1 stays open until its independent operational acceptance criteria are met.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**State:** ready-for-agent, explicitly requested by the maintainer. This means the specification is ready; dependency or runtime gates are not implied to have passed.
**Summary:** Persist bounded provider diagnostics without raw protocol capture by default

**Current behavior:**
Provider session reports retain captured stdout, stderr fragments and some exception messages. The host wrapper persists that report without a diagnostic projection, and initialization objects may carry unchecked extra fields. Cancellation messages can reach journals/outcomes. Native source-read errors already have a limited safe projection, but that protection does not cover the provider-report path. Actual credential exposure or public disclosure is not established.

**Desired behavior:**
Persist bounded, structured diagnostic summaries by default, preserving the origin, phase, classification and lifecycle/provenance facts needed to explain failures without retaining raw protocol streams, arbitrary exception text or unchecked metadata. Keep validated Council result payloads and required private identity bindings distinct from diagnostic logging.

**Key interfaces:**

- Provider session reports, wrapper readiness/result artifacts and `runHostWrapper()`.
- `readFailure()`, `PilotJournal`, cancellation results, `PilotOutcome` and `verifyContextResult()`.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Use fake provider and native-boundary fixtures with distinct synthetic canaries in stdout payloads, stderr, extra initialization keys and injected exception text. Reproduce current retention without any real credential or live provider.
- [ ] After the change, those diagnostic canaries do not appear in persisted diagnostic fields, wrapper fallback/cancellation/journal propagation or surfaced error strings. Validated user-requested Council result payloads remain usable.
- [ ] Retain allowlisted origin, phase, classification/code, input-delivery state and original exit/signal facts. Unknown values remain explicit; absent metadata never proves empty tools or successful containment.
- [ ] Define and test finite encoded-size limits for each persisted diagnostic summary, at and beyond the boundary. Truncation/omission is explicit, including multi-chunk input.
- [ ] Assignment, packet/control hashes, report/native completion binding and cleanup verification remain valid. Redaction cannot turn failure into success or bypass input gates. Version any required persisted contract change explicitly.
- [ ] Preserve restrictive ownership/file modes and existing journals. Add portable regressions for stdout/stderr/extra-key/exception and cancellation/fallback paths, then obtain independent review of the actual data-flow change.

**Out of scope:**

- Historical artifact deletion or rewriting, unrelated packet/result/archive retention and new raw-capture/forensics modes.
- Provider settings/trust changes, cleanup timing fixes or claims that a real confidentiality incident occurred.

**Execution and delivery:**
Work against a revision containing the relevant PR #2 implementation. Recheck the current tree and host policy. Supply portable offline coverage and a reviewable change or validation record, with fresh independent review of material work. Required live evidence must use already-authorized, qualified routes and finite declared call/deadline limits. If a required external capability or permission is unavailable, retain a precise blocker and leave operational completion open; do not substitute a diagnostics-only result for the requested behavior. No global settings, accounts, historical artifacts or unrelated work may be changed under this brief.


**Dependencies:** No sibling prerequisite. Runtime and authorization gates in the brief still apply.
